items.title: EntropyStrip: finding hidden payloads when naive Shannon entropy misses them https://github.com/dwexi/entropystrip @secharvester
items.one_liner: EntropyStrip is a new CLI triage tool for detecting concealed payloads in Windows PE binaries by overcoming Shannon entropy dilution.
items.summary: EntropyStrip is a newly released fast CLI tool designed for Windows PE triage, sliding-window entropy analysis, and the detection of concealed payloads in loaders and crypters. Traditional tools often miss hidden payloads due to section-wide Shannon entropy dilution caused by zero padding, NOP sleds, or string staging techniques like UUID and IPv4 arrays. EntropyStrip addresses these blind spots through sub-section inspection, modal byte distribution checks, memory permission flagging (W+X), Rich Header analysis, and automated payload dumping for disassembly in tools like Ghidra.
key_facts: Supported OS: Windows, Linux, or macOS
items.bottom_line: EntropyStrip provides security analysts with a sliding-window entropy analysis and payload-carving CLI tool to detect hidden shellcode masked by padding and string staging in Windows PE binaries.

items.title: Forgetting is Not Always Bad: A Neuro-Inspired Memory Repair Mechanism for Poisoned LLM Agents
items.one_liner: DREAM is a neuro-inspired, training-free memory repair framework that protects LLM agents from backdoor and poisoning attacks with high efficiency.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced DREAM (Dynamic Reactivation for Engram Attenuation in Memory), a training-free memory repair framework designed to protect LLM agents against memory-poisoning and backdoor attacks. Inspired by neuroscientific memory reconsolidation, DREAM operates via a three-stage pipeline involving perturbation-induced implicit reactivation, adaptive anomaly diagnosis using activation patterns, and dynamic memory repair that suppresses malicious entries while reinforcing benign ones. Experiments show DREAM reduces attack success rates by over 95% against backdoor poisoning while achieving up to a 2.13x speedup and 37.7% token reduction compared to existing baselines like A-MemGuard. The framework effectively secures multi-agent systems and maintains high task utility without external isolation modules.
key_facts: Framework Name: DREAM (Dynamic Reactivation for Engram Attenuation in Memory)
items.bottom_line: LLM agents can effectively mitigate memory-poisoning attacks without external audit modules by using neuro-inspired selective forgetting frameworks like DREAM.

items.one_liner: JANUS uses co-evolving world models to forecast and prune paths for long-horizon autonomous AI research agents.
items.summary: Researchers proposed JANUS, a framework to enhance long-horizon autonomous scientific research by combining future forecasting and past reflection via a co-evolving world model. Operating inside an evolving graph, the world model scores candidate branches on value improvement and information gain before tool execution, pruning inefficient paths. Evaluations on MLS-Bench-Lite show that JANUS outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both evolutionary efficiency and performance ceiling.
items.bottom_line: Co-evolving world models mitigate feedback delays in autonomous AI research by pre-evaluating hypotheses before costly execution steps.

items.title: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
items.one_liner: Web$hell provides a unified interface and caching architecture to streamline agentic web access, navigation, and research tasks.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced Web$hell, a unified interface designed to handle agentic web access across search-augmented, browser-based, and filesystem-based models. By utilizing a schema called WebContract, WebCompiler compiles live webpages into addressable information and action objects stored in WebCache, giving LLM agents a persistent and consistent interface. Experiments across web search, navigation, and deep research benchmarks demonstrate that Web$hell achieves high task performance at a lower operational cost.
items.bottom_line: Web$hell unifies fragmented web access paradigms for LLM agents into a single persistent cache and compiler architecture, improving efficiency.
